claims.text: Monolithic CoCrFeNi exhibits temperature-dependent variation in friction and wear.
The temperature-dependent tribological behavior of monolithic CoCrFeNi is caused by its lack of a built-in self-lubricating mechanism.
Uniformly distributed self-lubricating secondary-phase particles will promote formation of a tribofilm during sliding.
The resulting tribofilm will remain continuous and stable from room temperature to 800 °C.
Sliding and thermal activation will cause the secondary phase to release or transform into a lubricious agent.
The lubricious agent will cover the contacting surfaces and create a tribofilm.
The tribofilm will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact.
Reduced direct metal-to-metal contact will lower friction.
Reduced direct metal-to-metal contact will lower wear.
Modified CoCrFeNi will have a consistently lower coefficient of friction than monolithic CoCrFeNi throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
Modified CoCrFeNi will have a consistently lower wear rate than monolithic CoCrFeNi throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
Extreme loads may destabilize the secondary phase and limit its effectiveness.
Highly aggressive oxidizing environments may limit the effectiveness of the secondary phase.
At temperatures approaching or exceeding 800 °C, degradation or incompatibility of the secondary phase may limit effectiveness.
